title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, report controls and service-side auto-labeling entitlement are supported. It correctly distinguishes the government-cloud roadmap rollout from Learn's preview documentation and leaves report-specific defaults and automation unconfirmed.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview auto-labeling per-policy coverage report.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Auto-labeling per-policy coverage report

claims.claim: Admins can compare files processed during policy enforcement with the latest simulation run.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled

claims.claim: The report shows volumes of files not yet labeled.
claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled

claims.claim: The report indicates whether files were included in the latest simulation snapshot.
claims.quote: and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot.

claims.claim: The report identifies files processed during enforcement but absent from the simulation snapshot.
claims.quote: while also identifying files that were not found in the simulation snapshot but were processed during enforcement.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The selected policy must have completed simulation before coverage is reviewed.
claims.quote: Select an auto-labeling policy that includes SharePoint or OneDrive, has completed simulation, and is turned on.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The policy must be turned on after simulation before coverage is reviewed.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode, then turn it on before reviewing coverage.

claims.claim: The coverage route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Coverage > View coverage.
claims.quote: go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy; In the Coverage column, select View coverage.

claims.claim: Policy review pages are reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves labeling progress for the named policy.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to view. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the policy. For example: Name; IncludeProgressFeedback specifies whether to include the labeling progress of files in SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: The progress command reports enabled SharePoint and OneDrive labeling progress rather than coverage correlated with simulation.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.

claims.quote: and isn't intended to be an exact reconciliation between simulation and enforcement.

claims.claim: All-time labeled totals can differ because they include activity outside the coverage window.
claims.quote: All-time labeled totals can include activity from before or after the coverage window, so they might not match the counts shown in the coverage report.

claims.claim: A simulation match does not establish successful label application.
claims.quote: A simulation match doesn't prove that classification used the latest SIT definition or that enforcement will successfully label the file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report displays labeling outcomes; labeling is performed by the enabled policy rather than by opening the report.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode, then turn it on before reviewing coverage. The coverage report helps you see which files were labeled, pending, or not labeled, and whether those files were found in the latest simulation run.
